prereg.title: Discovery Screen 1: which neurons does the fly need to eat and to drink?
prereg.brain: FlyWire v783, published wiring and settings (same as round 1; engine v2 only adds a record of spike times, the maths is unchanged).
prereg.candidates: The 200 most active neurons when sugar neurons fire at 100/s plus the 200 most active when water neurons fire at 200/s (from the round 1 records), leaving out the sugar and water sensors themselves and MN9: 286 neurons.
prereg.method: Silence each candidate on its own (all its outgoing connections set to zero, as in the published code) and run sugar 100/s, then water 200/s. 10 repeats each for the screen. Every neuron scored 'needed' is then re-run with 30 repeats, and only the 30-repeat result is reported.
prereg.needed_rule: A neuron is 'needed' for eating (or drinking) if silencing it lowers MN9's firing by more than 20% compared with the unsilenced run with the same repeats (the 2024 study's threshold).
prereg.status_rule: Each predicted neuron is marked 'tested in the 2024 study' if it appears in that study's named neuron lists, otherwise 'no living-fly test known to us'. We do not claim no one has ever tested it.
prereg.not_claimed: These are predictions of a wiring-only model whose known track record is shown on the page. They are not facts about real flies until a living-fly experiment tests them.

summary: Discovery Screen 1: 286 neurons switched off one at a time on the FlyWire brain. 8 predicted needed for eating or drinking (MN9 more than 20% lower, confirmed with 30 repeats); 3 of them have no living-fly test known to the lab.
caveat_html: How much to trust these predictions. They come from wiring plus a simple neuron model. On known results this brain matched 10 of 15 checks, and the original study's predictions held up in 91% of 164 living-fly tests, but its misses were exactly the kind of single-neuron question this screen asks. Treat each line as a well-founded hypothesis, not a fact. "No test known to us" means we didn't find one; it doesn't mean no one ever tested it.

confidence_rule.written: 2026-11-03, after the screen; it labels results and changes none of them
confidence_rule.sim: Clear in the simulation if the 95% range of the drop (from 30 paired runs) stays above the 20% "needed" line.
confidence_rule.size: Large effect if the drop is 50% or more; moderate if 20-50%.

levels.1: Weak lead: the 95% range dips below the 20% line

confidence_rule.track: On known single-neuron silencing results, the model matched 2 of 4 when whole cell types were silenced (round 1, E6) and 3 of 4 one cell at a time in this screen (G2N-1 only just). Even a strong lead is a hypothesis.
